newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev dips at close despite c.bank support.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev dips at close despite c.bank support.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 218-219 per dollar, softer than 217.00/80 in morning trade despite central bank support as foreign currency demand topped supply on the interbank market, dealers said.

"The market was calmer than yesterday but (dollar) demand generally outweighed supply and could have pushed the lev even further down if it was not for dollar sales by the central bank," a commercial bank dealer said.
Traders said the central bank sold dollars at 217.50-218 lev in the morning, but raised its asks for the dollar to 219 levs as demand pressured the lev to 221 in the early afternoon. @
Central bank official were not available for comment.

A second postponement of International Monetary Fund (IMF) funding increased pressure on the lev this week as banks and final client bought foreign currency to square positions after sales in the past two weeks, dealers said.

Bulgaria's Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov said on Saturday that the IMF would not release the second $115 million tranche of funding, first delayed in September, until Bulgaria speeds up privatisation and closes down loss-making enterprises. @

Prevailing dollar-bullish sentiment boosted the lev to 212-213 per dollar at Friday's close from 236-237 on September 23 when the central bank hiked its main rate to 300 percent from 108 percent in a bid to support the fragile local currency. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
